items.title: Section: The Ālaya Untouched by Affliction, and Manas Never Free of Its Own Four

items.zh: 復次，阿賴耶識無有煩惱而共相應。末那恒與四種任運煩惱相應，於一切時俱起不絕。謂我我所行薩迦耶見、我慢、我愛、不共無明。是諸煩惱，與善、不善、無記識俱而不相違。其性唯是隱沒無記，任運而起。當知諸餘分別所起，隨眾緣力差別而轉。
items.en: Furthermore, the ālaya-consciousness has no affliction associated with it at all. Manas is constantly associated with four effortlessly arising afflictions, present continuously at all times: the view of self and what belongs to self, self-pride, self-love, and unshared constant ignorance. These afflictions coexist with wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral consciousness without contradiction, their own nature being hidden and undetermined, arising effortlessly. One should know that all other afflictions, arising through discrimination, turn according to the differing power of their own conditions.

items.zh: 又與末那相應俱有遍行任運四種煩惱，世間治道尚不能為損伏對治。何以故？已離欲者猶現行故，隨所生處，是諸煩惱即此地攝。當知此地已離欲者，此地煩惱現行不絕。何以故？

items.title: Section: Why No Worldly Path Can Touch Manas's Own Four, and the Ground Possessing Mind Closes

items.zh: 此諸煩惱，唯阿賴耶識種子所引，於一切時任運而生，非所對治及能對治境界緣力差別轉故。諸離欲者，世間治道若現在前、若不現前，此諸煩惱現行不絕。若諸有學已見迹者，出世間道現在前時，此諸煩惱不得現行。從彼出已，還復現行。善通達故，未永斷故。若諸無學，此一切種皆不現行。是諸煩惱，當知唯離非想非非想處欲故，一時頓斷。非如餘惑漸漸而斷。如是等類，當知是名建立雜染、清淨差別。於此地中餘決擇文，更不復現。如是已說有心地決擇。無心地決擇，我今當說。
items.en: These afflictions are drawn only from the ālaya-consciousness's own seed, arising effortlessly at all times, not turning according to the differing power of objects and conditions the way the afflictions to be counteracted and the path that counteracts them do. For trainees who have already seen the path, when the transcendent path manifests, these afflictions do not manifest; once that state is left, they manifest again. For the fully trained, none of these manifest at all, in any respect. One should know these afflictions are cut all at once, only upon leaving desire for the base of neither perception nor non-perception, not gradually as other afflictions are cut. The remaining decisive-discernment texts on this ground will not appear again. The decisive discernment of the Ground without mind. Thus I have already explained the decisive discernment of the Ground possessing mind. I shall now explain the decisive discernment of the Ground without mind.

items.title: Section: A Sixth Ground Opens — Seven Reasons Mind Sometimes Fails to Arise at All

items.zh: 問：心不生因，凡有幾種？由幾種因，心不得生？答：心不生因，略有七種；由此因故，心不得生。何等為七？謂緣闕故，心不得生；如是作意闕故、未得故、相違故、斷故、滅故、已生故，心不得生。
items.en: Question: how many causes prevent mind from arising? Through how many causes does mind fail to arise? Answer: the causes preventing mind from arising are, briefly, seven; through these causes, mind fails to arise. What are the seven? Through deficiency of conditions, mind fails to arise; likewise through deficiency of attention, through not yet having attained it, through opposition, through being cut off, through being extinguished, and through having already arisen, mind fails to arise.

items.zh: 云何由緣闕故，心不得生？

items.title: Section: A Faculty Left Undamaged Still Sees Nothing Without Attention

items.zh: 謂內眼處壞，若外色處不現在前；廣說乃至內意處壞，若外法處不現在前；爾時由彼所生眼識乃至意識終不得生。如是名為由緣闕故，心不得生。云何作意闕故，心不得生？謂雖有內眼處不壞，外色處現前；廣說乃至內意處不壞，外法處現前；若無能生作意正起，爾時由彼所生眼識乃至意識終不得生。如是名為作意闕故，心不得生。云何由未得故，心不得生？謂如有一，於下欲界思惟麁相，於初靜慮思惟靜相，為欲證得初靜慮故。若於此道不極作意，若修、若習、若多修習，不善修故，於初靜慮未能證得；由未得故，初靜慮俱心不得生。
items.en: When the eye faculty is damaged, or its external object of form is not present, and so on through the mind faculty and its object, the corresponding consciousness, from eye consciousness through mind consciousness, ultimately fails to arise. Though the eye faculty is undamaged and its object present, and so on, if no attention capable of giving rise to consciousness actually arises, the corresponding consciousness ultimately fails to arise. As when one contemplates the coarse mark of the desire realm below and the still mark of the first absorption, wishing to attain the first absorption. If insufficient effort, practice, or repeated practice is applied, and it is not skilfully cultivated, the first absorption is not attained; because it is not attained, the mind belonging to the first absorption fails to arise.

items.zh: 又如有一，於初靜慮、第二、第三、第四靜慮、空無邊處、識無邊處、無所有處思惟麁相，於第二靜慮乃至非想非非想處思惟靜相，如前廣說。又如有一，遍於一切薩迦耶中思惟苦相，於薩迦耶滅涅槃界思惟靜相；為斷一切薩迦耶故，為欲證得涅槃界故。若於此道不極作意，若修、若習、若多修習，不善修故，不能盡證一切涅槃；由未證故，於諸結、縛，及與隨眠、隨煩惱、纏永解脫心便不得生。如是名為由未得故，心不得生。云何由相違故，心不得生？

items.title: Section: Why Joy and Grief Cannot Share a Single Moment

items.zh: 謂如有一，觸能隨順樂受諸觸，受樂受時，樂受相應心現在前；爾時苦受、非苦樂受相應之心，以相違故，便不得生。如是若觸能順苦受、不苦不樂受觸，如前廣說；爾時樂受、非苦樂受，樂受、苦受相應之心，以相違故，便不得生。又如有一，貪纏所纏，貪纏相應心現在前；爾時瞋纏相應之心，以相違故，便不得生。如是若有瞋纏所纏，廣說乃至爾時貪纏相應之心，以相違故，便不得生。如是名為由相違故，心不得生。云何斷故，心不得生？
items.en: As when one experiences contact that accords with pleasant feeling, and while experiencing pleasant feeling, the mind corresponding to pleasant feeling stands present; at that time, the minds corresponding to painful feeling and to neither painful nor pleasant feeling, being opposed to it, fail to arise. As when one is bound by the entanglement of greed, and the mind corresponding to that entanglement stands present; at that time, the mind corresponding to the entanglement of hatred, being opposed to it, fails to arise.

items.title: Section: Permanent Cutting-Off, Cessation Temporary and Final, and a Mind That Never Arises Twice

items.zh: 謂如有一，由善修習八聖支道故，證得無餘貪欲、瞋恚、愚癡永盡；彼於爾時，有貪、有瞋、有癡心等隨一心法，諸隨煩惱所染污心，彼由已斷、已遍知故，皆不得生。如是名為由永斷故，心不得生。云何滅故，心不得生？謂如有一，生無想天、入無想定、入滅盡定；於其中間經爾所時，由斷滅故，心不得生。又如有一，於無餘依涅槃界中已般涅槃；彼於爾時，畢竟滅故，心不得生。如是名為由滅盡故，心不得生。云何由已生故，心不得生？所謂一切已生之心，於現在生剎那已後，必成滅法。彼現在時，由已生故，便不可生。彼若滅已，亦已生故，終不可生。如是名為由已生故，心不得生。應知由此七因緣故，心不得生。與此相違七因緣故，隨其所應，諸心得生。
items.en: As when one, through thoroughly cultivating the noble eightfold path, attains the complete and final end of greed, hatred, and delusion; at that time, no mind of greed, hatred, delusion, or any secondary affliction can arise, since these have already been severed and fully known. As when one is born into the heaven of no-thought, enters the attainment of no-thought, or enters the attainment of cessation; for the duration of that state, through interruption, mind fails to arise. As when one has entered nirvana without residue; at that time, through final extinguishing, mind fails to arise. Every mind already arisen necessarily perishes in the moment following its present arising. One should know that through these seven causes, mind fails to arise. Through their exact reverse, mind arises accordingly.

items.zh: 謂緣不闕故、作意不闕故、已證得故、不相違故、未斷滅故、未滅盡故、未已生故。於此地中餘決擇文，更不復現。

blocks.text: Manas and its four constant afflictions, and the seven reasons a mind may fail to arise.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the view of self joined with manas is innate; its ignorance is "constantly active unshared ignorance". These afflictions arise spontaneously, even when one does wholesome things: self-delusion, self-view, self-pride, and self-love are present too.

Master Cháng Bǎi: worldly absorption treats only afflictions that vary with objects. For learners the four are subdued in non-conceptual wisdom, but their seeds are not cut, so after emerging they appear again. Only the arhat has cut them. (Untranslated, 0651c20: even those free of desire still have them active, belonging to whatever level they are born in.)

subs.head: Seven reasons mind does not arise

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: if a seed has already manifested, it will not arise again as that same moment.

Master Cháng Bǎi: if the mind has no attention to see, hear, or know, consciousness does not arise; one looks without seeing. Practice done poorly does not attain the first meditation. (Untranslated, 0652a28: one who contemplates the coarse and calm aspects of each level, or suffering in all the self-view and peace in nirvāṇa, but without full attention, does not reach complete release.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: with greed the mind wishes to join its object, with hatred to part from it, so the two do not manifest together.

Master Cháng Bǎi: one who has cut the seeds of affliction will not see them arise again. In some states consciousness is only interrupted; in nirvāṇa without remainder its causes are ended. (Untranslated, 0652c08: the seven reasons summarised; no further text for this stage.)
The meditations analysed, then the mind's deepest layers: the ālaya, always neutral, and manas, always clinging. Even in wholesome acts, until arhatship, the sense of "I" is quietly present.

quiz.q: With which four spontaneous afflictions is manas constantly associated?
options: the view of self and what belongs to self, self-pride, self-love, and unshared ignorance
greed, hatred, delusion, and pride, the root afflictions
anger, enmity, concealment, spite
dullness, restlessness, faithlessness, laziness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the view of self here is the innate kind joined with manas; its ignorance is called constantly active unshared ignorance. The four differ from afflictions arising through discrimination, which are named just after in the treatise.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish spontaneous afflictions from those arising through discrimination?
options: spontaneous ones are learned in life, and discriminative ones are innate
spontaneous is good, discriminative evil
spontaneous ones appear of themselves without discriminating; discriminative ones in the six vary with objects
spontaneous is form realm, discriminative desire realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: spontaneous afflictions need no discrimination and appear of themselves; the six consciousnesses have discriminative afflictions that vary with objects. The treatise says those others turn according to the differing power of conditions.

quiz.q: How do manas's four afflictions relate to wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral consciousness, and what is their nature?
options: they join only unwholesome consciousness, stopping at good thoughts
they coexist with all three without contradiction, their nature being hidden and undetermined
they join only neutral consciousness
they join only wholesome consciousness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when doing unwholesome things, self-delusion, self-view, self-pride, and self-love are present too. The treatise states this for wholesome and neutral minds as well. The lecture reads 隱沒 two ways, so its meaning is not tested.

quiz.q: This is rendered "the way what they oppose and what opposes them do." What is wrong with the relation?
options: nothing: both clauses mean the noble path, repeated for emphasis, as the lecture says
所對治 is discriminative affliction and 能對治 the noble path, while the English points both at the path
境界 should be "realms"
緣力 should be "willpower"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: worldly absorption treats only discriminative afflictions that vary by object; the transcendent path that treats them is not spontaneous either. So one side is what is treated, and the English loses it. This is his explanation of the missing context.

quiz.q: How are the four afflictions of manas cut?
options: gradually, a part with each realm left, like all other afflictions
all at once, only on leaving desire for the highest formless sphere, not gradually like others
all at the path of seeing
all at the first absorption
quiz.why: The subject is the four afflictions of manas alone. Master Cháng Bǎi: the adept has finally cut seeds of craving and view, acquired and innate. His reference to vajra-like concentration is his addition; the treatise speaks of leaving the highest formless sphere.

quiz.q: What happens to manas's four afflictions for trainees during and after the transcendent path?
options: during it they are cut forever and never return, trainees equaling adepts
they grow during it and weaken after
during it they are subdued and do not manifest; the seeds being uncut, they manifest afterwards
they are unaffected either way
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: at that time self-delusion, self-view, self-pride, and self-love are temporarily subdued; their seeds are not cut, so after leaving non-conceptual wisdom they manifest again. The treatise's own reason is missing, so this rests on his words.

quiz.q: What are the seven causes of mind not arising?
options: ignorance through feeling, the first seven links of dependent origination
deficient conditions, deficient attention, not attained, opposition, cut off, extinguished, already arisen
the five hindrances with evil conduct and wrong view
the seven underlying tendencies
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi on the last: if a seed has already manifested, of course it will not arise again. The seven names are given only in this section; the English omits the headings below, so later questions supply the matching themselves.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say the first cause, deficient conditions, refers to?
options: attention not arising, so nothing occurs though faculty and object exist
affliction being cut
entering cessation
the faculty being damaged or the object absent, since consciousness needs both to arise
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: deficient conditions here means specifically that the faculty is damaged or the object absent; for consciousness to arise and discern, it must rest on a faculty and take an object. Option B is the second cause.

quiz.q: What example does the treatise give for the third cause, not attained?
options: when pleasant feeling is present painful feeling does not arise, not being attained for the moment
the first absorption is not well cultivated and not attained, so its mind fails to arise
greed does not arise in an arhat
mind does not arise in non-perception
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though there is practice, it is not done well or skilfully, so the first absorption is not attained, and the moment of mind joined with its five factors does not arise. The treatise's other examples of this cause are missing from the English.

quiz.q: With the fourth cause, opposition, what happens while experiencing pleasant feeling?
options: the minds of painful and of neutral feeling, being opposed, fail to arise
all three arise together, the ālaya having neutral feeling
only pain fails, and neutral feeling arises
pleasant feeling turns into pain
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: feeling pleasure, the mind joined with it is present, and minds of pain and neutral feeling, being opposed, do not arise. This concerns transforming consciousnesses and does not conflict with the ālaya's constant neutral feeling in §30.

quiz.q: Why does a mind of hatred not arise when one of greed is present, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: they are one affliction under two names, so no second arises
greed wants to join with its object and hatred to part from it, so hatred does not appear with greed
hatred is weaker than greed
greed is good and hatred evil
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with greed the mind wishes to join its object, and with hatred to part from it, so while greed is present hatred does not manifest. Their directions are opposite. The reverse case is missing from the English, though the principle extends to it.

quiz.q: Why can a mind of greed no longer arise in one who has ended greed, hatred, and delusion?
options: through opposition: a wholesome mind simply keeps it out for the time
through deficient conditions: objects being absent
through deficient attention: no attention being present
through being cut: they have been severed and fully known
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: such a person has cut the seeds of affliction and fully knows the four truths, so no affliction arises again; here it is because seeds are forever cut that mind does not arise. Opposition, by contrast, is only temporary.
